summary: Phase B-3 Time Tracking full-stack review. Backend: 2/2 pytest cases green (test_time_entries.py — CRUD/validation/rollup/my-week + rate snapshot isolation). Frontend E2E on /team/time and /accounting/projects/:id → Time tab both work end-to-end: log form saves, day-grouped list renders, filters (project + billable) apply, delete confirms and removes rows, weekly strip shows Monday-anchored 7 day cards (time-week-day-*) with prev/today/next nav. Project Time tab correctly locks the project select (disabled=true), pre-fills the project, and the 4 rollup KPI cards + by_phase + by_employee tables refresh after logging (Total hours 1.25→3.75, tables render, delete returns count 2→1). Regressions clean: WelcomeModal no longer overlays the dashboard on this session (previously z-[900] blocker from iter77 is gone), all 4 ProductRail items (accounting/crm/team/projects) render and product-rail-team clicked through to /team. Sidebar Team→Time link present. Project notes block (Phase B-2) still renders on ProjectDetail Overview.

design_issues.screen: /team/time & Project Time tab (Bright Beans Coffee Co.)
issues: Sarah K employee has hourly_cost_rate=0/null so all Labor cost / Billable value rollups display $0.00 — not a bug, but E1 may want to seed a non-zero cost rate on demo employees so the KPI cards look meaningful in demos.

action_items: (Optional) Seed a non-zero hourly_cost_rate on demo employees (e.g. Sarah K in Bright Beans) so labor cost / billable value rollup cards render non-$0.00 during demos.

(Optional) The my-week status line 'Not linked to an employee — logging shows entries you created' shows for pro@axiom.ai (no employee row in Bright Beans). This is by design per the fallback in my_week (uses created_by_user_id). Cosmetically fine, worth confirming that's the intended messaging.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/time_entries.py is clean, well-documented, and correctly excludes MongoDB _id via _clean() on every write/read path.

PATCH endpoint order-of-operation: if the caller passes BOTH phase_id and project_id in the same PATCH body and the project changes, the phase set by the `phase_id` branch is IMMEDIATELY overwritten to null by the project_id branch (because dict update). This is the correct/documented behavior (phase belongs to one project) but the earlier phase validation call `_load_phase(cid, payload['phase_id'])` becomes wasted work + still 400s if the phase existed under the *old* project. Minor: consider swapping the order (project_id branch first) so a mixed payload isn't paying for a phase lookup that will be discarded.
list_time_entries default limit=500 with le=2000 — fine for MVP; add pagination cursor once companies exceed ~2k entries per query window.

my-week fallback to created_by_user_id is smart, but note that a Pro user who has logged entries for OTHER employees in the past week will see those entries under 'my-week' too. UX text ('logging shows entries you created') is honest about this, but could confuse if the manager expects only 'my' hours.
cost_rate_snapshot correctly frozen at write time (line 156-157) — rate-change isolation test proves this. Good design.

No permission check beyond require_company — any member of the company can create/edit/delete anyone else's time entry. Acceptable for MVP but flag once role-scoped time approvals are added in Phase B-4.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on happy path (/team/time + Project Time tab + regressions)
